# My Broken Boat

> Outboard Help: free, plain-English troubleshooting for common outboard boat motor problems. Each page has a short quick answer, likely causes, safe owner checks, parts/tools, when to call a marine mechanic, and source citations. General information only; specs are model-specific, so follow the owner's manual. When in doubt, see a marine mechanic.

## Won't start

- [Why won't my outboard crank when I turn the key?](https://mybrokenboat.com/problems/wont-crank/): Most often: kill-switch lanyard not attached, not in neutral (neutral safety switch), weak/dead battery. Start here: Confirm lanyard clip is seated on the stop switch. If that doesn't fix it, work through the checks below, and see a marine mechanic if you're unsure.
- [Why does my outboard crank but not start?](https://mybrokenboat.com/problems/cranks-wont-fire/): Most often: fuel not reaching engine: tank vent closed, empty tank, line not connected, primer bulb not pumped, clogged fuel filter / tank filter, stale or contaminated fuel. Start here: Open tank vent; confirm fuel level; reconnect hose fittings at both ends. If that doesn't fix it, work through the checks below, and see a marine mechanic if you're unsure.
- [Why does my outboard start and then die?](https://mybrokenboat.com/problems/starts-then-dies/): Most often: tank vent closed (vacuum builds), primer bulb/check valve failing or air leak in fuel line, partially clogged filter or carb idle jet. Start here: Open vent; loosen cap — if it runs on, vent was the cause. If that doesn't fix it, work through the checks below, and see a marine mechanic if you're unsure.
- [How do I fix outboard choke or enrichment problems?](https://mybrokenboat.com/problems/choke-enrichment/): Most often: cold start without choke/prime, choke left on after warm-up (flooding, soot), using choke on an already-warm engine. Start here: Follow your manual's cold-start sequence. Tohatsu small 4-strokes, for example: choke fully out, throttle to START, pull; push choke back once running; choke not needed when warm. If that doesn't fix it, work through the checks below, and see a marine mechanic if you're unsure.
- [Why won't my outboard pull-start cord work?](https://mybrokenboat.com/problems/pull-start-recoil/): Most often: not in neutral (start-in-gear lockout), rope won't retract: rewind spring slipped from slot, weak, or broken, starter housing bolt over-tightened after reinstall. Start here: Shift to neutral and retry. If that doesn't fix it, work through the checks below, and see a marine mechanic if you're unsure.

## Runs poorly

- [Why does my outboard idle rough or surge?](https://mybrokenboat.com/problems/rough-idle/): Most often: gummed carb idle circuit (after storage), fouled plug / misfiring cylinder, air leak in fuel supply. Start here: Try fresh fuel with stabilizer/cleaner per label. If that doesn't fix it, work through the checks below, and see a marine mechanic if you're unsure.
- [Why does my outboard bog or stall when I throttle up?](https://mybrokenboat.com/problems/stalls-under-throttle/): Most often: fuel starvation: clogged filter, vent closed, kinked line, weak bulb, gummed carb main/accelerator circuit, water in fuel. Start here: Open vent, straighten hose, pump bulb while accelerating — improvement = supply issue. If that doesn't fix it, work through the checks below, and see a marine mechanic if you're unsure.
- [Why has my outboard lost power or won't plane?](https://mybrokenboat.com/problems/loss-of-power-wont-plane/): Most often: trim too far in/out, too much load or poor weight distribution, damaged or wrong-pitch prop, spun hub, fuel restriction. Start here: Check for warning lights first (overheat/oil/low-pressure modes cut power). If that doesn't fix it, work through the checks below, and see a marine mechanic if you're unsure.
- [Why does my prop slip, ventilate, or cavitate?](https://mybrokenboat.com/problems/prop-cavitation-ventilation/): Most often: trimmed out too far (ventilation), engine mounted too high on transom, damaged prop or gearcase, missing diffuser ring. Start here: Trim down and re-test. If that doesn't fix it, work through the checks below, and see a marine mechanic if you're unsure.
- [Why is my outboard smoking so much?](https://mybrokenboat.com/problems/excessive-smoke/): Most often: normal briefly after fogging or during break-in (Tohatsu: double-oil break-in mix makes more smoke), 2-stroke oil mix too rich / oil injection fault, choke left on, poor carburetor adjustment, wrong spark plug. Start here: Note when and what colour: right after storage or break-in may be normal. If that doesn't fix it, work through the checks below, and see a marine mechanic if you're unsure.
- [Why do my outboard spark plugs keep fouling?](https://mybrokenboat.com/problems/spark-plug-fouling/): Most often: long idling/trolling, wrong plug heat range, too rich (choke, carb). Start here: Use plug type in manual (Honda notes wrong heat range can trigger overheat warning). If that doesn't fix it, work through the checks below, and see a marine mechanic if you're unsure.

## Overheating & cooling

- [Why is there no tell-tale (pee) stream from my outboard?](https://mybrokenboat.com/problems/no-telltale-stream/): Most often: telltale outlet plugged by debris/insects/salt, lower-unit water intake screens blocked (weeds, mud, bag), worn/failed water pump impeller. Start here: Shut engine off promptly if alarm or no stream. If that doesn't fix it, work through the checks below, and see a marine mechanic if you're unsure.
- [Why is my outboard overheating or sounding the alarm?](https://mybrokenboat.com/problems/overheating-alarm/): Most often: blocked water intake, failed impeller, stuck thermostat. Start here: Throttle down, neutral, shut off. Don't "baby it home." If that doesn't fix it, work through the checks below, and see a marine mechanic if you're unsure.
- [How often should I replace my outboard water pump impeller?](https://mybrokenboat.com/problems/water-pump-impeller/): Inspect the water pump impeller every year and replace it every 1 to 3 seasons, or right away if the motor overheated or ran dry. Suzuki's guideline is inspect at 200 hours or 1 year and replace at 300 hours or 3 years; Mercury lists 300 hours or 3 years on many models; many mechanics replace it every season or two in salt, sandy or muddy water. Your owner's manual interval wins.

## Fuel problems

- [How do I tell if there's water in my outboard fuel?](https://mybrokenboat.com/problems/water-in-fuel/): Most often: condensation in vented tank, ethanol phase separation, leaking fuel fitting/line (odor). Start here: FUEL SMELL: stop, no sparks/smoking, ventilate, find leak before running. If that doesn't fix it, work through the checks below, and see a marine mechanic if you're unsure.
- [How do I fix a carburetor gummed up after storage?](https://mybrokenboat.com/problems/carb-gummed-after-storage/): Most often: old fuel evaporated, leaving varnish in jets, fuel left in carb bowl without stabilizer, ethanol attacking fuel parts. Start here: Drain carb bowl (manual procedure) and refill with fresh fuel. If that doesn't fix it, work through the checks below, and see a marine mechanic if you're unsure.
- [What problems does ethanol (E10) fuel cause in outboards?](https://mybrokenboat.com/problems/ethanol-fuel-issues/): Most often: e10 absorbs water → phase separation, e10 solvent action loosens tank debris into filters, incompatible old fiberglass tanks/hoses. Start here: Never use above E10 in outboards (Mercury, Honda). If that doesn't fix it, work through the checks below, and see a marine mechanic if you're unsure.
- [Why won't my primer bulb firm up?](https://mybrokenboat.com/problems/primer-bulb/): Most often: air leak: loose connector or bad O-ring at quick-connect, failed check valves in bulb (installed backwards or worn), cracked hose or bulb. Start here: Bulb arrow points toward engine. If that doesn't fix it, work through the checks below, and see a marine mechanic if you're unsure.

## Electrical & controls

- [Why is my outboard battery not charging?](https://mybrokenboat.com/problems/battery-charging/): Most often: loose battery cables (vibration loosens nuts) — techs say most engine problems are fuel or battery, corroded terminals, battery left connected/discharging between trips. Start here: Wiggle each cable at the terminal — it should not budge; tighten if it does. If that doesn't fix it, work through the checks below, and see a marine mechanic if you're unsure.
- [Why isn't my power trim/tilt working?](https://mybrokenboat.com/problems/trim-tilt/): Most often: blown PTT fuse, weak battery / loose or corroded connections, manual release valve not fully closed or leaking (appears in most rows of Suzuki's table). Start here: Check battery voltage and connections. If that doesn't fix it, work through the checks below, and see a marine mechanic if you're unsure.
- [Why is my outboard hard to shift or not shifting?](https://mybrokenboat.com/problems/shifting-problems/): Most often: shifting at above idle RPM, helm-to-engine shift cable stiff, kinked, or tight-radius bends, corrosion/binding at the engine-side linkage. Start here: Only shift at idle, with a firm, decisive motion. If that doesn't fix it, work through the checks below, and see a marine mechanic if you're unsure.
- [Is my kill switch or lanyard stopping my outboard?](https://mybrokenboat.com/problems/kill-switch-lanyard/): Most often: lanyard clip missing/loose, wrong clip type, corroded/damaged stop switch or wiring. Start here: Attach lanyard and clip fully. If that doesn't fix it, work through the checks below, and see a marine mechanic if you're unsure.
- [Why is my outboard beeping?](https://mybrokenboat.com/problems/warning-horn-beeping/): A beeping outboard is a warning, not a glitch: throttle back, shift to neutral, and read the warning light or display. A continuous horn usually means a critical problem like overheating, low oil pressure, or no cooling water, so stop the engine and check. Short intermittent beeps usually mean something less urgent, like water in the fuel filter or low oil level. One short beep at key-on is a normal self-test.

## Seasonal care

- [How do I winterize an outboard motor?](https://mybrokenboat.com/problems/winterizing/): Start here: Stabilize fuel and run in water so it circulates (Honda: ~10 min). If that doesn't fix it, work through the checks below, and see a marine mechanic if you're unsure.
- [How do I start my outboard after winter storage?](https://mybrokenboat.com/problems/spring-startup/): Start here: Inspect fuel lines, bulb, clamps for cracks; replace hardened lines. If that doesn't fix it, work through the checks below, and see a marine mechanic if you're unsure.
- [Why is my outboard gear oil milky?](https://mybrokenboat.com/problems/gear-oil-milky/): Most often: prop shaft seal damaged by fishing line, worn seals, drain/vent screw gasket bad. Start here: Check prop shaft for fishing line. If that doesn't fix it, work through the checks below, and see a marine mechanic if you're unsure.

## Emergencies

- [What do I do if my outboard was submerged?](https://mybrokenboat.com/problems/submerged-motor/): Most often: water in cylinders and electrics. Start here: Do not try to start it — risk of hydrolock. If that doesn't fix it, work through the checks below, and see a marine mechanic if you're unsure.
